Thank you Madam Chair, Terry Schmidt, General Manager of Transportation and Construction and Good afternoon committee members.
This report provides an update on the status of Saskatoon Transit Fairbox Operations and Reliability.
In 2022, Saskatoon Transit face challenges related to the reliability of the legacy Fairbox System known as Payment and Payment and Motion or PIM.
This system went live in February 2010 and knowing upgrades were required three years ago.
Saskatoon Transit went to the market to find a solution to provide mobile ticketing technology to the residents of Saskatoon.
To procurement process resulted in the purchase and implementation of the Mesabi Mobile ticketing system.
The Mesabi system implementation involves two phases.
Phase one went live in June 2021 and included the mobile phone-based Fair Payment System,
but not the cards required to transition to Mesabi Card-based Fair Collection.
To date 43% of rides tracked electronically were with mobile ticketing.
In late 2022, upgrades were made to the PIM system as well to upgrade to a more modern version of the system as the vendor was no longer servicing the system in place.
Retaining and upgrading the PIM system was necessary in part because the PIM system accepts cash and printed transferred required for cash fairs.
Retaining both systems allowed all types of fairs to continue to be utilized during the transition period to the full Mesabi system.
Although there were periods of time throughout 2022 where many buses did not have full Fairbox capability,
every bus now has fully functional Fairboxes and any issues or failures that occur are dealt with through maintenance.
The Mesabi system has proven to be reliable experiencing only a few isolated incidences where an onboard validator had to be serviced.
A major component of phase two implementation of the Mesabi system will be adding the Card Fair Payment option to complement the existing mobile phone payment option.
Implementing the Mesabi Card Payment System will require not only system change but policy considerations as well.
Since the city will be fully transitioning from the product-based ticketing PIM system to a cash account-based ticketing system.
This change will require public engagement and outlet city council approval as it will change how fairs are collected and may require changes to bylaw 8370 the transit fair bylaw 24204.
Examples that will require further attention and process changes include the following three fair types in their current forms.
Income pass, the discounted pass and the cash fair collection.

For each two of the Mesabi planning implementation was deferred primarily due to the fact that Saskatoon transit staff were fully dedicated to providing continued service during the pandemic and did not have the capacity to contact the public engagement bylaw reviews.
In the spring of 2023, Saskatoon transit plans to recommence with phase two implementation of the Mesabi mobile ticketing.
Phase two will involve collaboration with several departments.
Public engagement policy and bylaw review could take 12 to 18 months to complete followed by report to committee and council with options and recommendations.
Phase two implementation will not include a fair review as this will be dependent on upcoming work.

Administration was directed to undertake a development of a council policy on user fees and subsidies to clearly identify principles and objectives on where to charge fees and offer subsidies and report back to the appropriate committee.
No later than Q4 of 2023.
Saskatoon transit is in process of hiring electronic technician position that will be dedicated to repair and servicing of fair box technology and other IT technology on buses.
This will better position Saskatoon transit to consistently maintain fair box and IT functionality on a goal forward basis across the fleet.
Saskatoon transit will continue installing the new PIM smart card and cash fair boxes in the remaining fleet.
As of writing of this report, 80 buses of 130 bus fleet have had the new equipment installed.
It is planned to have the new PIM smart card and cash fair boxes installed in the entire fleet by early April 2023.

There are two types of fair issues experienced by Saskatoon transit, unpaid fairs and fair evasion.
Unpaid fairs are transit fairs that have not been paid by a rider on a fixed route bus due to either a missing or an operable fair box.
Fair evasion is transit fairs that have not been paid by a rider on a fixed route bus and working fair boxes are in place.

Unpaid fairs on Saskatoon transit are not tracked as there is no feasible way to determine if a person is boarding the bus with a valid fair card or cash for fair payment if there is no operable fair box available for payment.
Fair evasion is tracked by operators using the mobile data terminal or MDT on the bus.
